label: Person
name: John Blair Jr.
summary:
John Blair Jr. (1732–1800) was an American jurist and Founding Father from Virginia who served as an Associate Justice of the United States Supreme Court (1790–1795) — one of the original justices appointed by President Washington. Blair was a Virginia delegate to the Constitutional Convention (1787) and one of the men who signed the Constitution — making him both a framer and an inaugural Supreme Court justice. On the first Supreme Court under Chief Justice John Jay, Blair participated in the court's foundational early work including the establishment of circuit-riding duties and the early articulation of federal judicial power.

He was one of Virginia's most respected jurists — having served on the Virginia General Court and Virginia Court of Appeals before his elevation to the Supreme Court.

He was both a framer and a founder of the federal judiciary.

He signed the Constitution and served on the first Supreme Court.
